note: Evil Mode slice 11, the economy (design Part 12 sections 1 and 2, Part 13 sections 1 and 2, Part 5 sections 2.2 to 2.4). Kanto's hand-written Cards: six Rackets, five Fronts and four Works, each with the Honest Card's text (fields 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 12 and 13; the name, odds, who's going, who won't and not known are worked out from the block). `where` is the districts (n) a Card is offered in; empty is every district after the Arrival. `names` is the somebody field 3 names. `on: false` is the slice's undo: holdings pay flat takings, no Card is offered and a short Evening works as before. Upkeep lines come from running Works here; rooms add theirs when the base is built.

words.title: Trade
words.noStreet: No street the team holds a holding on.
words.warmStreet: {street} is Warm. "They'd not believe you meant it. Then they'd believe you. Don't."
words.notOnNeighbours: Not on neighbours. (Belonging runs no racket but the Tithe.)
words.creedOnly: Only a Cause or Belonging team keeps a Tithe.
words.line: Shut by your Line: {line} doesn't work a racket.
words.arrival: Nobody's earned anything yet. Rackets wait for the first district.
words.dispatchOnly: Trade's done at Dispatch: a squad's day.
words.already: {street} already has a racket on it.
words.noHolding: A Front needs a holding the team has by deed, lease or share: one it Paid for or was given (Persuade).
words.needs: Nobody free has {talent}. Every Front needs someone of the talent it's for.
words.noSquad: Nobody free to go who'd go.
words.short: Not enough Funds: {cost} needed, {funds} in hand.
words.waived: {name}: today's takings waived. The street's a day more patient.
words.endedEarly: {name} is ended, early. {street}: "They stopped. On their own." Each one warmer.
words.shut: {street}'s Shut. {name} is over. Heat +{heat}. What would turn there, turned.
words.broke: Somebody on {street} has had enough alone: {act}
acts: somebody's painted a word on the safehouse door.
the baker's shut. Not the shop: himself. He's gone to his sister's.
Mr. Onuoha's sitting outside the constable's. He's not gone in. He's sitting.
words.frozen: {street} pays. Nobody goes to the constable.
words.leftBehind: {name} on {street} ends with the district: nobody's there to collect.
words.feedEnds: Feed the District ends with the district.
words.noBackRoom: There isn't one. Think about why.
words.runWell: {name} was run well this district. Regard +{n}.
words.straight: Going Straight: {n} of {of} Fronts in profit with the back room shut a whole district.
words.short1: Short. Wages are paid late. Nothing falls yet. Everyone knows.
words.short2: Broke. Wages aren't paid. Loyalty −1 for those paid least: {names}.
words.whipOnce: The Whip-Round's been held this region.
words.whipRegard: Only with Regard 4 or more: the district has to like you enough to put money in a tin.
words.sold: {name} is sold for {amount}. They were told the truth at Night.
words.whip: The district pays the team's wages for a day: {amount}, in a tin. The Boss stands in the Mess and takes it. Loyalty +{n}, everyone.
words.hint: Up/Down picks a Card. Left/Right changes the tab. P changes the street or holding. Enter does it (the button is under field 13). V waives, E ends, M makes honest, B shuts or opens a back room. Esc closes.

written.lastJob: Robbed a payroll van. A week's wages, from forty people at the mill.
written.sell: Sold {name}, and told them the truth.
written.whip: The district paid the team's wages for a day. Line by line, with names: {names}.

text.takes: ₽300 a day, each, from eight boats on {street}.
text.from: Eight fishing families, Mr. Rafael Zamora's boat the eleventh in the row. They clear about ₽900 a day each.
text.moves: Heat: stays while it's the day's loudest (a floor). Dread +1 at the start. Regard −1 a week. The fish market's prices rise: every local here pays more for supper.
text.holds: Turns. The street goes with it.
text.hero: Their uncle fishes from this dock.
text.written: Took a third of eight families' living, daily, for nothing.
text.other: Buy the cannery from Mr. Baumgartner (₽12,000; pays ₽3,000 a day, clean; it out-earns the racket inside five days). The boats sell to it gladly.

honest.name: The Cannery
honest.says: They bought it. They pay what Harland paid, and on Fridays.
honest.written: Bought the cannery. The boats sell to it.

text.takes: The Game Corner on {street}, with the odds leaned on.
text.from: Whoever plays. Mr. Bartholomew Quaye, the mill foreman, loses more than he's got by the third night.
text.moves: Heat +1 more at the start. Dread +1. Regard −1 with everyone who's lost.
text.hero: They'll win a Porygon here, fairly or not. They'll notice which.
text.written: Leaned on the odds at the Game Corner. A man lost his wages to it.
text.other: Run it straight: ₽1,800 a day, and it's a Front. Side by side: ₽4,000 crooked, ₽1,800 straight.

honest.name: The Corner, straight
honest.says: I lost ₽40. Fairly. I'd forgotten what that was like.

text.takes: A street pays to be left alone, by the team: four or five businesses on {street}.
text.from: Four or five businesses; Mrs. Ifeoma Castellanos of the Anchor pays first, so the others will.
text.moves: Dread +1 at the start, and +1 a week.
text.hero: They'll ask who the street's paying. Somebody will tell them.
text.written: Charged a street to be left alone by us.
text.other: Actually protect it: from the neighbour, from the Alpha on the hill. Then it's a wage: ₽1,000 a day, the street's Easy, and it holds.

honest.name: The Watch
honest.says: The other lot came on Tuesday. Ours saw them off. I've never said 'ours' about anyone before.
honest.written: Kept the street's watch, for a wage.

text.takes: Loans at a rate, to whoever's short on {street}: ₽300 a borrower, rising.
text.from: Four borrowers. Miss Marisela Oyelaran, 19, who's running her dad's stall since he took ill, is the first.
text.moves: Dread +1 at the start. Each borrower's fear becomes "the team."
text.hero: One of the borrowers is the Hero's mother's friend.
text.written: Lent to people who were short, at a rate they couldn't pay.
text.other: Lend at cost: the Mutual (₽2,000 and a float of ₽3,000). ₽100 a borrower. They pay it back.

honest.name: The Mutual
honest.says: I paid it back in March. I've borrowed again. I'm not ashamed to.
honest.written: Lent at cost. They paid it back.

text.takes: Every Poké Ball in {town} sold by one shop, at double.
text.from: Every trainer in town. Mrs. Wen Li-Hua's bicycle shop stops stocking them.
text.moves: Dread +1 at the start. Regard −2. Children can't start out.
text.hero: The Hero can't afford Balls here. Their team's a Pokémon short for the district.
text.written: Bought up every Poké Ball in town and sold them at double.
text.other: Open a second shop that undercuts. It's competition. It's allowed. ₽900 a day.

honest.name: Two shops
honest.says: The new place does a loyalty stamp.
honest.written: Opened a second shop that undercuts the first.

text.takes: A tenth: ₽150 a head, from members and friendly locals on {street}.
text.from: Everyone on the Roster, by name, and the locals who like the team.
text.moves: Loyalty steady while they believe. It doesn't frighten anybody: no Dread, no Heat.
text.hero: The Hero hears it's a church. It isn't, quite.
text.written: Took a tenth from our own.
text.other: Tell them what it's spent on. In full. The Ledger, open, in the Hall. Then Loyalty +1, and it's a subscription.

honest.name: The Subscription
honest.says: I read the whole Ledger. There's a line for the kettle.
honest.written: Opened the Ledger in the Hall. Every line.

text.takes: ₽2,500 to open, and {person} in the kitchen.
text.from: The float. Miss Dilys Okpara sells it bread at cost; she likes to be asked.
text.gives: ₽800 a day, clean: logged as trade.
text.moves: Regard +1. Heat: none; a Front's quiet.
text.holds: Holds. Against the Hero, and against the team's own bankruptcy: a Front's the last thing sold.
text.hero: The Hero eats there. Twice. They like the soup.
text.written: Opened a café. It's a good café.
text.other: The quicker way: a racket on the same street pays twice as much from day one, until the street's patience runs out.

text.from: The float. Miss Juniper Achebe, the teacher, sends the first three children.
text.gives: ₽600 a day, clean. Applicants +1 a district.
text.moves: Heat: none. The Holding Pen can't be in the same building, or anywhere in the district.
text.hero: The detective's niece is on the waiting list.
text.other: The quicker way: the Café opens for ₽500 less and pays ₽200 more.

text.takes: ₽1,500 to open, and {person} on its books.
text.from: The float. Mr. Caspian Nwachukwu at the bank holds its account.
text.moves: Regard +2. Heat: none. Its back room moves Funds between districts without a van.
text.holds: Holds. It's audited, and it passes, if it's run well.
text.written: Opened a charity. The books balance.
text.other: The quicker way: hand the ₽1,500 out at the Town tonight. Regard +1, once, and nothing after.

text.takes: ₽3,000 to open, and {person} under the cars.
text.from: The float. Mr. Oswin Takahashi-Bello brings his carts on the first day.
text.moves: Heat: none. Its back room's plates and paint: a van's a different van by morning.
text.hero: An old man brings a bicycle every week that isn't broken. The Hero's seen him.
text.written: Opened a garage. A real one.
text.other: The quicker way: steal the vans you need. Heat +3 each.

text.takes: ₽1,000 to open, and {person} with a hoe.
text.from: The float. Mrs. Philippa Mwangi lends the ground behind her cottages.
text.moves: Heat: none. Its back room's a shed.
text.hero: People who'd never speak to the team stand next to its Grunts with a hoe. The Hero's grandmother is one.
text.written: Dug allotments and gave out the plots.
text.other: The quicker way: buy the vegetables. ₽200 a day, and no shed.

text.takes: ₽4,000 of the team's, and two days.
text.from: The float. Mrs. Chiamaka Eze has run the ferry under it since it fell.
text.gives: Nothing a day. Nugget Bridge stands again.
text.moves: Regard +2. Heat −2, once, for the first Work in a district. Loyalty +1, everyone with Heart, Doubts or Kind.
text.hero: The Hero crosses it. Somebody's put a plaque on it by then. It doesn't say who paid.
text.other: The quicker way: charge a toll on the bridge as it is. ₽1,500 a day, and the Hero finds the ford.

text.takes: ₽3,000 of the team's, and a day.
text.from: The float. Mr. Gaspard Okonjo, the watchman, walks it with them.
text.gives: Nothing a day. Lamps on every street in {town}.
text.moves: Regard +2. Heat −2, once, for the first Work in a district. Loyalty +1, everyone with Heart, Doubts or Kind.
text.hero: They walk home under it. Somebody asks why the team did it.
text.other: The quicker way: light only the street the team works. ₽1,000, and nobody asks why.

text.from: The float. Mrs. Yewande Halloran lends the hall and her big pot.
text.moves: Loyalty +1, everyone, at the start. Regard +1 a week.
text.hero: Somebody in the queue's a Grunt's mother. The Hero's in it too, once.
text.other: The quicker way: feed only the team. ₽150 a day, and no queue.

text.takes: ₽5,000 of the team's, and three days.
text.from: The float. Dr. Anselm Whitlock-Sato, the only doctor in three districts, takes the second room.
text.gives: Nothing a day. Free healing, for anyone. Including the Hero.
text.moves: Regard +2. Heat −2, once, for the first Work in a district. Loyalty +1, everyone with Heart, Doubts or Kind.
text.hero: The detective comes in with a sick Growlithe. It's treated. They say thank you.
text.written: Opened a clinic. Anyone can come.
text.other: The quicker way: a racket on the district's medicine pays ₽2,000 a day. The Center runs short.

text.from: A week's wages, from forty people at the mill. Mr. Bartholomew Quaye, the foreman, signs for it.
text.hero: Their friend's mother works the carding room. She won't be paid this week.
text.written: Robbed a payroll van. A week's wages, from forty people at the mill.
text.other: Sell a Front, and tell them the truth at Night. Or: ask the district (the Whip-Round, from Regard 4).

text.takes: {name}, the last thing a team sells.
text.from: The team. {person} runs it, and will hear tonight.
text.gives: {amount}, once, and no more takings from it.
text.holds: It holds: it's somebody else's now.
text.hero: They'll see a new name over the door.
text.written: Sold {name}, and told them the truth.
text.other: Ask the district (the Whip-Round, from Regard 4). Or One Last Job.

text.takes: A day's wages, from the district: {amount}.
text.from: Locals who were helped, in person, with a tin: {names}. Most of the names are small amounts.
text.moves: Loyalty +1, everyone. The Boss has to stand in the Mess and take it.
text.hero: Somebody who put in tells the Hero. They don't know what to make of it.
text.written: The district paid the team's wages for a day.
text.other: One Last Job. Or sell a Front.
